newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Survey shows rise in Brazil roasted coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows rise in Brazil roasted coffee sales.

text.p: A survey by Brazil's Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union of 12 companies showed a rise in roasted coffee sales of 21.4 percent in April compared with March and of 5.8 percent on April 1996, the union said.

"The new price levels achieved after the adjustments of February and March, helped by the end of the summer and colder days, has allowed industries to see a strong recuperation in sales," union president Nathan Herszkowicz said in a statement. During the first four months of this year, sales totalled 692,000 bags, a rise of seven percent on January to April 1996.
In the twelve-month period to April 1997, sales by the 12 firms were 15.6 percent higher than in the corresponding period in 1995/96, reaching 2.19 million bags.
"If this pattern continues, it is highly probable that the Brazilian coffee industry will meet its goal of processing 12 million bags in 1997 against 11 million bags last year," said Herszkowicz.
